definitions.gloss: kudzu vine (Pueraria montana); the plant itself
definitions.explanation: A vigorous climbing vine native to East Asia. One of the {秋|あき}の{七草|ななくさ} (seven autumn flowers) in Japan; the root is harvested for food and medicine.
A fine white starch made from the root of the kudzu plant. Used in traditional Japanese sweets and to thicken sauces. Sometimes labeled in English as "kuzu".

examples.english: The kudzu vines are in flower.

examples.japanese: {葛|くず}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{秋|あき}→秋：02276_aki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{七草|ななくさ}→七草：11190_nanakusa⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一|ひと}つ→一つ：02948_hitotsu⟧だ。
examples.english: Kudzu is one of the seven flowers of autumn.

examples.japanese: ⟦{裏|うら}→裏：02178_ura⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{山|やま}→山：02168_yama⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{葛|くず}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{一面|いちめん}→一面：11184_ichimen⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{広|ひろ}がっている→広がる：01980_hirogaru⟧。

examples.japanese: {本|ほん}{葛|くず}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{高級|こうきゅう}→高級：08644_koukyuu⟧な⟦{和菓子|わがし}→和菓子：04962_wagashi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{使|つか}われる→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。

examples.english: Dissolve kudzu in water and add it to hot dashi to make a smooth thickened sauce.

notes:
Do not confuse with ⟦{屑|くず}→屑：03883_kuzu⟧ (scrap, trash, worthless person), which is a homophone written with a different kanji. The two have nothing to do with each other semantically.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {葛|くず}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{根|ね}→根：03525_ne⟧: kudzu root
- {本|ほん}{葛|くず}: pure kudzu starch (high grade)
- {葛|くず}{粉|こ}: kudzu powder
- {葛|くず}{湯|ゆ}: hot kudzu drink (sweetened thickened starch)
- {葛|くず}{餅|もち}: kudzu starch mochi (traditional sweet)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Kudzu is one of the ⟦{秋|あき}→秋：02276_aki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{七草|ななくさ}→七草：11190_nanakusa⟧ (seven autumn flowers) celebrated in classical Japanese poetry. The starch made from its root has been valued in cuisine and traditional medicine for centuries.
